content.text: {"label":"none","explanation":"The payments staffing alert (26 vs 31 expected) is mostly caused by our own earlier actions, not by a real supply problem. Three cross-skilled payments agents were moved to general from 09:30 to 12:00. Payments breaks from 10:00-11:30 were also delayed 30 minutes, so they are now falling around 11:30-12:00, which matches the dip in agents on phones (28 at 11:30, 24 at 11:45). Attendance shows 0 absences logged on either queue (usual is about 2). There are no customer-facing incidents and no marketing entries. Service level is healthy: payments 91.9% and general 97.3% in the latest interval. Volume is above forecast today (payments +14%, general +27%), but recent payments intervals are back on forecast. The general excess is mainly balance_enquiry, which is already being deflected to chat, and existing overtime and callback cover it. No disruption needs a new intervention.","plan_name":"Hold and monitor","rationale":"Both queues are well above the 80/20 target. The 5-agent payments gap is temporary and self-inflicted. The cross-skill move ends at 12:00, which returns 3 agents, and the delayed breaks are finishing. Payments overtime runs to 12:30 and coaching is cancelled to 12:30. General already has overtime to 13:45, callback to 14:00 and chat deflection to 14:00. Adding levers now would spend overtime budget or use up the one-delay-per-agent break allowance for no service benefit. Re-check at the next interval, and consider a payments overtime offer only if service level falls below about 85% or volume climbs again.","actions":[]}
